anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > The centre of gravity > Worked Example 1: Locating the centre of gravity: "Therefore, the centre of gravity lies between the thick base and the 0.60 m midpoint."
title: Locating the Centre of Gravity in Non-Uniform Objects
action: Select the correct statement describing the location of the centre of gravity of a flat triangular metal sheet that is thickest at one corner and thinnest at the opposite edge.
prompt: A triangular metal sheet has uneven thickness: it is very thick and heavy at corner P and tapers to a thin edge at the opposite side. Where is its centre of gravity located relative to its geometric center?

options.text: Closer to corner P than to the geometric center, because the centre of gravity shifts toward the region of greater mass concentration.
Exactly at the geometric center, because the centre of gravity of any flat shape always coincides with its geometric center.
Outside the perimeter of the sheet, because uneven mass distribution forces the centre of gravity outside flat objects.
Closer to the thin opposite edge, because a smaller mass requires a larger distance to balance the heavy corner.

feedback.A: Correct. The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight may be considered to act. In non-uniform objects, it shifts toward the region with higher mass concentration (corner P).
feedback.B: Incorrect. The centre of gravity coincides with the geometric center only for uniform objects with symmetrical mass distribution. Here the mass is concentrated near corner P.
feedback.C: Incorrect. While the centre of gravity can lie outside hollow bodies like rings, a solid flat triangular sheet has its centre of gravity within its boundaries, shifted toward the heavier corner.
feedback.D: Incorrect. This confuses the balance point of an object with the distance of an external load on a lever. The centre of gravity itself shifts toward the region containing more mass.

anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > Defining the moment of a force > Worked Example 2: Calculating a direct moment: "A downward push to the right of the pivot tends to turn the spanner clockwise."
title: SI Units and Dimensions of a Moment
action: Select the option that correctly states both the coherent SI unit and the SI base units of the moment of a force.
prompt: Which row correctly identifies the defining formula, coherent SI unit, and SI base units for the moment of a force?

options.text: Formula: M = F d_perp; Coherent SI unit: N m; SI base units: kg m^2 s^-2
Formula: M = F / d_perp; Coherent SI unit: N m^-1; SI base units: kg s^-2
Formula: M = F d_perp; Coherent SI unit: J; SI base units: kg m^2 s^-2
Formula: M = F d_perp; Coherent SI unit: N m; SI base units: kg m s^-2

feedback.A: Correct. Moment is the product of force (N) and perpendicular distance (m), giving N m. Since 1 N = 1 kg m s^-2, multiplying by m gives kg m^2 s^-2.
feedback.B: Incorrect. Moment is the product of force and perpendicular distance, not force divided by distance. N m^-1 is the unit of spring constant or surface tension.
feedback.C: Incorrect. Although 1 N m has the same base dimensions as 1 joule (kg m^2 s^-2), the joule is reserved exclusively for energy and work. A moment is a rotational turning tendency, never measured in joules.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The base units kg m s^-2 correspond to force (newtons) alone. Multiplying force by distance in metres introduces another factor of m, yielding kg m^2 s^-2.

anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > Forces that produce zero moment > Worked Example 3: Force directed through a pivot: "The length of the rod does not create a moment because it is parallel to the force."
title: Identifying Forces with Zero Moment
action: Select the force that exerts zero moment about the pivot P.
prompt: A horizontal uniform beam is pivoted at its left end P. Four forces A, B, C, and D act on the beam. Which force exerts zero moment about pivot P?

options.text: A vertical downward force acting at the right-hand end of the beam.
A horizontal pulling force directed away from P along the longitudinal axis of the beam.
An upward force acting at the midpoint of the beam at 45 degrees to the horizontal.
A vertical downward force acting at the centre of gravity of the beam.

feedback.A: Incorrect. This force has a vertical line of action located at a non-zero perpendicular distance (the entire length of the beam) from P, producing a clockwise moment.
feedback.B: Correct. The line of action of this force extends along the longitudinal axis of the beam and passes directly through pivot P. Therefore, its perpendicular distance from P is zero (d_perp = 0 m), producing zero moment.
feedback.C: Incorrect. Although angled at 45 degrees, its line of action does not pass through P; it has a non-zero perpendicular distance from P and therefore produces an anticlockwise moment.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The downward weight acting at the centre of gravity has a vertical line of action separated horizontally from P, exerting a non-zero clockwise moment.

anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > The turning effect of an object's weight > Worked Example 4: Moment of a horizontal beam's weight: "The downward weight force therefore tends to rotate the beam clockwise about the pivot."
title: Calculating the Moment of an Object's Weight
action: Calculate the moment produced by the weight of a non-uniform bar about pivot P.
prompt: A non-uniform bar has a mass of 0.50 kg. Its centre of gravity G is located 0.30 m from end A. The bar is supported horizontally by a pivot P located 0.18 m from end A. Using g = 9.81 N kg^-1, what is the magnitude and rotational sense of the moment of the bar's weight about pivot P?

options.text: 0.59 N m clockwise
0.59 N m anticlockwise
0.060 N m clockwise
1.47 N m clockwise

feedback.A: Correct. Weight W = m g = 0.50 kg x 9.81 N kg^-1 = 4.905 N. The perpendicular distance from pivot P to the vertical line of action through G is 0.30 m - 0.18 m = 0.12 m. Moment M = 4.905 N x 0.12 m = 0.5886 N m approx 0.59 N m. Because G is to the right of P, downward weight produces a clockwise moment.
feedback.B: Incorrect. The magnitude is calculated correctly, but the rotational sense is inverted. Since G is at 0.30 m and P is at 0.18 m from end A, G lies to the right of P. A downward force on the right tends to rotate the bar clockwise.
feedback.C: Incorrect. This uses mass (0.50 kg) directly in the moment formula without multiplying by gravitational field strength g (9.81 N kg^-1): 0.50 x 0.12 = 0.060. Weight in newtons must always be used.
feedback.D: Incorrect. This uses the entire distance of G from end A (0.30 m) instead of the distance from the pivot P (0.30 m - 0.18 m = 0.12 m): 4.905 N x 0.30 m = 1.47 N m. Moments must always be calculated using the distance to the pivot.

anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > Perpendicular distance for angled bodies and forces > Worked Example 5: Moment of an inclined sign: "Because the weight pulls downward to the right of hinge H, the moment acts clockwise."
title: Perpendicular Distance in Angled Geometries
action: Identify the correct perpendicular distance expression for an inclined beam.
prompt: A uniform beam of length L is hinged to a vertical wall at its bottom end and held at an angle theta to the vertical. Its weight W acts vertically downward through its midpoint (distance L/2 from the hinge). What is the perpendicular distance d_perp from the hinge to the line of action of the weight?

options.text: d_perp = (L/2) sin theta
d_perp = (L/2) cos theta
d_perp = L/2
d_perp = (L/2) tan theta

feedback.A: Correct. The weight acts along a vertical line. The perpendicular distance from the hinge to this vertical line is horizontal. In a right-angled triangle where the beam forms the hypotenuse of length L/2 and theta is the angle to the vertical, the horizontal side opposite theta is (L/2) sin theta.
feedback.B: Incorrect. (L/2) cos theta represents the vertical component along the wall (adjacent to theta), not the horizontal perpendicular distance to the vertical weight line.
feedback.C: Incorrect. L/2 is the slanted distance along the beam to the centre of gravity. Perpendicular distance must meet the vertical line of action at 90 degrees.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle is L/2. The opposite side is found using sine (hypotenuse x sin theta), not tangent.

anchor: Centre of gravity and the moment of a force > Solving for force or distance > Worked Example 6: Rearranging for force and distance: "The unit newtons cancels out, leaving metres."
title: Algebraic Rearrangement and Unit Cancellation
action: Select the correct algebraic rearrangement and unit calculation to find perpendicular distance.
prompt: A technician applies a force of 25 N to produce a required moment of 7.5 N m about a pivot. Which expression correctly calculates the perpendicular distance d_perp and verifies unit cancellation?

options.text: d_perp = M / F = 7.5 N m / 25 N = 0.30 m, where newtons cancel leaving metres.
d_perp = F / M = 25 N / 7.5 N m = 3.3 m^-1, where newtons cancel leaving inverse metres.
d_perp = M x F = 7.5 N m x 25 N = 190 N^2 m, where units multiply.
d_perp = M / F = 7.5 N m / 25 N = 0.30 N m^-1, leaving newtons per metre.

feedback.A: Correct. Starting from M = F d_perp, dividing both sides by F yields d_perp = M / F. Substituting the values gives 7.5 N m / 25 N = 0.30 m. The newton units cancel, leaving metres.
feedback.B: Incorrect. This inverts the algebraic division (calculating F / M instead of M / F). The resulting unit is m^-1, which is not a distance.
feedback.C: Incorrect. Multiplying moment by force gives N^2 m, not distance. To isolate distance, you must divide by force.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The numerical value is correct, but the unit is wrong. In the division (N m) / N, newtons cancel out, leaving m, not N m^-1.
